start_here: Say to your AI: "Check that the files attached to these incoming messages are really in my Files before you take them in." It runs tool:check-incoming-attachments on the batch and hands it back with each attachment's real name and media type.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it only looks each attached file up in the account's Files and fills in what it found.
instructions: 1. Gather the batch of arrivals or messages as items, each naming its attachments by their Files identity (1f: and 64 hex characters).
2. Say "Check these attachments"; the AI runs tool:check-incoming-attachments with {items}.
3. Each distinct identity is looked up once in your Files; the name and media type the carrier claimed are replaced by the file's own.
4. If any identity is missing, malformed or not in your Files, the whole batch is refused before anything is taken in, and the message says which file.

worked_examples.title: A forged attachment name is replaced by the file's own name and type
worked_examples.ask: Check the attachment on this incoming message before keeping it.
worked_examples.given: From tools/bring-in-what-i-write-elsewhere/test/incoming-files.test.mjs (first test): the account's Files hold that identity as /Kept/true.wav, an audio/wav file. The answer below is the item that test asserts after the check.
